mappings.note: Whose mother the poet blesses and why -- both halves are answered from the poem's narrative situation. Rejected LO-7 because no image, ras or shilp feature is analysed.
Why the crop is called 'nadiyon ke paani ka jaadu' -- justifying a metaphor, i.e. kala-paksh. Rejected LO-6, which fits the recall form naming water as the agent (item 78).

Define 'mitti ka gundharm' -- the poem uses it as a rupak for the crop itself, so the answer is image interpretation. Rejected LO-6 because a literal soil-science definition is not what the poem means.
Explain HOW the smile puts life into a corpse -- unpacking an atishayokti and its bhaav. Rejected LO-6, which takes the recall form of this line (item 49).
Prove the poem expresses the effect of shishu-SAUNDARYA -- kaavya-saundarya and bhaav-paksh outright. Rejected LO-6 because the demand is an argued aesthetic reading, not comprehension.
How the smile revives the dead -- the same atishayokti explained. Rejected LO-6 for the same reason as its twin item 124; this is a verbatim duplicate of that question.

What the human contribution is to the crop growing and bearing -- the poem's stated content about collective labour. Rejected LO-7 because the answer recounts the poem's argument rather than its shilp or saundarya.
How air, sun, water and people each contribute -- an inventory drawn straight from 'Fasal'. Rejected LO-7 as no figurative expression is being interpreted. (Stem has the OCR artefact 'fasaalon'.)
